# C1 coverage ledger

Snapshot: 2026-11-03. **Provisional: C1 is not complete.** The release and plan prose review and semantic reconciliation of the retained release leads remain open (PROMISES.md, Reading scope and remaining review). These counts measure this ledger, not proof that all product behavior has been found.

One table below, ordered by section and capability home. Sources retain input row identities and line numbers. A journey appears once, in `journeys`, with its goal category and documentation/guide paths. The retired J09 remains traceable but is not a task to document. Several readers share one item; Covered by gives each reader's judgement. The row count uses the least complete reader judgement. `after 0.16` is a writing deferral for AI and agent features, not a statement that those features are unbuilt. Digests and workspace following are current, including the restored inventory's DOC9A-marked publication event.

Coverage is deliberately conservative. A page existing, or mentioning a label, does not establish full coverage. Exact setting/command table entries and the individually checked passages are marked covered; other existing homes remain partly pending a clause-by-clause reading. A partly row names the behavior in Item whose full treatment still needs checking; it is not a verified diagnosis of a particular missing sentence. Pending release leads are evidence to reconcile, not current product promises. Semantic duplicates beyond exact statements and explicit source aliases remain to merge. Do not use these counts as a final writing brief until that work is complete.

Source files: PROMISES.md (primary record and unreconciled evidence), BEHAVIOUR-RULES.md, OUTLINE.md, NOT-YET-COVERED.md, MODEL-EDITOR-INVENTORY.md, UI-INVENTORY-SETTINGS.md, UI-INVENTORY-DATA.md, ../_coverage/restored/INVENTORY.md, docs/product-functionality/USER_JOURNEYS.md. NOT-YET-COVERED.md is an older audit: some pages it called absent now exist. Its claims are checks to resolve, not facts to repeat. Existing guide pages were indexed by their complete current text and headings; coverage judgements do not imply that every page was manually read in full. Future homes follow OUTLINE.md and astro.config.mjs GROUPS.

| C0697 | Release evidence awaiting reconciliation: Rule: Two conditions on a relationship, and two stamps, so the list and the query mean the same. filter.related:<key>.under=<record ID> keeps records with some related record under that ancestor record at any depth, .notUnder=<record ID> those with none; each such entry must hold. They are the query's hop with an ancestor:<type> criterion, as set statements in PostgreSQL (list_relation_filters builds one hop per type the related records can stand under, each starting from the ID of that type only, so a wrong type selects nothing), live and in a change set or publication, and _related_predicate now accepts the ancestor criterion on its hop. The query and an export say the same with ancestor:<type> and not. The filter bar's relationship editor gets "has none under" and "has any under" with a record picker over the types the related records can stand under (read from the served placements), and a pill reads "has none under Webshop". createdAt and updatedAt filter every live table list without being declared, offered in + Filter, and not in a change set or publication, which record no times (UNRECORDED_TIMESTAMPS). A field with two conditions, such as the two ends of a date range, is a pill for each. No domain key anywhere.. The journey cannot be said otherwise, and a capability only the question could reach would be a defect (the API is the product). The list, selection, bulk actions and export read the one filter, so what the person sees is what is. | rule | steward | use | PROMISES.md unreconciled PL-AG-D33; PL §0.16 plan AG-D33 | uncovered → use/importing-and-exporting — reconcile the cited release evidence before writing |

Not on the workspace's Activity, which sits under Settings › Administration › Workspaces and which a reader may never reach. A change set published in a followed workspace, from an approved request or directly, puts a notice of the new kind change-set.published ("A change set was published in a workspace you follow") in each follower's inbox, but not the publisher's, in the publication's transaction, one INSERT … SELECT over the followers who still hold Browse there. From there it is a kind like the others: at once, in the digest or no mail (AO-D33), its line without names (AO-D31). Publications only, not withdrawals. People only: clients have the webhooks and the change feed. API: GET /me/followed-workspaces, PUT and DELETE /me/followed-workspaces/{workspaceKey} (404 for a workspace the person cannot Browse, repeat harmless). Migration: workspace_followers (user_id, workspace_key, created_at; both keys cascade).. Every other kind is about something that needs the person or is theirs; a publication is others' work, and the inbox keeps every notice (D434), so sending it to every reader would fill each reader's inbox with no way to stop it. | C1673 | Release evidence awaiting reconciliation: Rule: Which draft opens. (1) The remembered draft while it is current: its base is the release the workspace runs, or a release installed after the workspace's model last changed (an Apply stopped at the migration preview). (2) Otherwise the newest draft of the running release that remembers no workspace and that no assistant task names (ai_tasks.draft_id), whatever the task's state; it now remembers this workspace. (3) Otherwise a new draft of the running release, named "The model of ‹workspace›". A remembered draft that is no longer current, because the workspace's model was changed elsewhere, gives up the link and stays in Settings › Model.. Without (1)'s second half, leaving a migration preview would orphan the person's work. Without the last sentence, an old draft could silently undo someone else's activation. A finished task's draft is left out too: after an accept. | rule | steward | model | PROMISES.md unreconciled PL-WM-D2; PL §0.16 plan WM-D2 | after 0.16 |
